extracted.intended_audience: news organizations, journalists, fact-checkers, platform moderators, researchers and anyone evaluating news-source reliability
extracted.subtask_description: A rubric for scoring and rating the overall reliability of news websites/sources based on credibility and transparency criteria, with weighted points summing to a 0–100 score and banded interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not repeatedly publish false content
rubrics_metrics.description: Does not repeatedly publish false content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 22 points (part of the Credibility 60-point subtotal). Evaluates whether a source repeatedly publishes demonstrably false information. This is a high-weight criterion reflecting truthfulness and the absence of a pattern of publishing falsehoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathers and presents information responsibly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 18 points (part of the Credibility 60-point subtotal). Assesses sourcing, verification practices, balance, and whether reporting follows responsible journalistic methods when obtaining and presenting facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularly corrects or clarifies errors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 12.5 points (part of the Credibility 60-point subtotal). Looks for transparent correction policies and an observable pattern of issuing corrections or clarifications when errors occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Handles the difference between news and opinion responsibly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 12.5 points (part of the Credibility 60-point subtotal). Evaluates labeling and separation of factual reporting vs. opinion, analysis, or advocacy to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoids deceptive headlines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 10 points (part of the Credibility 60-point subtotal). Checks whether headlines accurately reflect story content, avoiding clickbait or misleading headline-content misalignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website discloses ownership and financing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 7.5 points (part of the Transparency 40-point subtotal). Requires that the site provides clear information about who owns it and how it is funded, so readers can assess potential influences or biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly labels advertising
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 7.5 points (part of the Transparency 40-point subtotal). Evaluates whether advertising is distinguishable from editorial content and clearly labeled to avoid confusing ads with news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals who's in charge, including any possible conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveals who's in charge, including any possible conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 5 points (part of the Transparency 40-point subtotal). Looks for disclosure of editors/management and any conflicts of interest that could affect coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides names of content creators with contact or biographical information
rubrics_metrics.description: The site provides names of content creators, along with either contact or biographical information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted at 5 points (part of the Transparency 40-point subtotal). Assesses whether authors/journalists are identified and whether readers can find basic background or contact information for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and interpretation (Score Bands)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sites scored 0–100 and interpreted with bands
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total score derived from weighted criteria (Credibility 60 + Transparency 40 = 100). Bands: 75%+ = Generally credible; 60–75% = Credible with exceptions; <60% = Unreliable. The rubric is used as a pass/fail style evaluation but presented as a numeric score and band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of assessment: sources not individual stories
rubrics_metrics.description: NewsGuard rates sources rather than individual stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rubric evaluates the overall practices and patterns of a news site (policies, transparency, correction behavior, sourcing), not each separate article. Scores reflect site-level reliability rather than story-level accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit newsworthiness and quality dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Underlying qualities the criteria target (truthfulness, verification, transparency, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists implicit criteria the rubric operationalizes: truthfulness (no false content), verification standards, error transparency, news/opinion distinction, headline-content alignment, funding transparency, ownership disclosure, author transparency, and ad-content distinction. These summarize the substantive aims driving the nine scored criteria.
